printed: ; os.inc -- one program, two operating systems.
; Include this FIRST. Assemble with -DHDOS for an HDOS 2.0 .ABS file or
; -DCPM for a Heath CP/M 2.2.04 .COM file. Your program supplies `main`
; (it may return, or call exit) and ends by including tail.inc.
; Both systems get the same routines:
;   conout   A = character out. Keeps BC, DE, HL.
;   conin    A = a key, NC; carry if no key is waiting. Keeps BC, DE, HL.
;   getkey   waits for a key; A = it.
;   exit     restore the console and return to the system.
;   args     HL -> the command line's arguments, NUL-terminated.
;   f_write  DE -> data, BC = length (any). Carry = failed.
;   f_read   DE -> buffer, BC = size; BC = bytes read, 0 at the end.
;   f_close  write what is buffered, close. Carry = failed.
;   TICKS    the word the system's 2 ms clock counts up.
TICKS           equ     0x201B          ; HDOS's tick counter (S.TIME area)
S_CSLMD         equ     0x20D6          ; the five console mode bytes
HDOS_EOS        equ     0x227F          ; the command line ends here (a NUL)
; system calls: RST 38H followed by the function number
defb    0xFF, 0x00              ; the .ABS header, 8 bytes, comes first
ld      (os_argp),sp            ; HDOS leaves SP on the command line
; raw character mode, no echo, no case mapping, no width: escape sequences
ld      hl,S_CSLMD              ; keep the console as we found it
ld      a,0                     ; S.CSLMD: echo off, raw, character mode
ld      a,1                     ; S.CONTY: no case mapping
ld      a,(os_consave)          ; put the console back as it was
; HL -> the arguments: from where SP pointed at entry to 227FH
ld      a,h                     ; SP was 2280H: no arguments
ld      hl,os_nul               ; none: an empty string (227FH
ret                             ;   holds a NUL only if there were)
; files: channel 0, read or written through a 256-byte sector buffer
ld      (f_scall+1),a           ; the SCALL number, patched in
SCALL   0                       ; OPENW or OPENR, A = channel 0
ld      a,h                     ; a whole sector: write it
ld      hl,(os_fcnt)            ; pad the last sector with zeros
ld      hl,(os_fcnt)            ; buffer empty? read a sector
SCALL   _READ                   ; carry: the end of the file
TICKS           equ     0x000B          ; the Heath BIOS's tick counter
CPM_TAIL        equ     0x0080          ; the command tail: length, text
ld      sp,os_stack             ; our own stack (the CCP's is tiny)
jp      0                       ; warm boot back to the CCP
; console through BDOS function 6, direct: no echo, no ^S or ^P
; HL -> the arguments: the CCP's command tail at 80H, made NUL-terminated
; files: one FCB, read or written through a 128-byte record buffer
ld      c,19                    ; delete any old one
ld      hl,os_fcb               ; clear it: drive 0, blank name
ld      a,l                     ; a whole record: write it
ld      hl,(os_fcnt)            ; pad the last record with ^Z
ld      hl,(os_fcnt)            ; buffer empty? read a record
ld      c,20                    ; read sequential: not 0 = the end
; fujinet.inc -- the H89 FujiNet card and the FujiBus protocol, as names.
; The card is an 82C55A at 0D0H (320Q): port A carries the bytes, port C
; the handshake and the lines that start the ESP32, and 0D3H is the
; control register. fncmd.inc (made from the firmware) names every device
PORTA           equ     0xD0    ; 82C55A port A: the byte pipe (mode 2)
PORTB           equ     0xD1    ; port B: wired to nothing; holds SETUP_MARK
PORTC           equ     0xD2    ; port C: status in, control out
PCTRL           equ     0xD3    ; control word / port C bit set-reset
PC_OBF          equ     0x80    ; PC7 /OBF: 1 = the byte we wrote was taken
PC_ACK          equ     0x40    ; PC6 /ACK (driven by the ESP32)
PC_IBF          equ     0x20    ; PC5 IBF: 1 = a byte from the ESP32 waits
PC_STB          equ     0x10    ; PC4 /STB (driven by the ESP32)
PC_EN           equ     0x04    ; PC2: ESP32 enable (1 = running)
PC_OE           equ     0x02    ; PC1: 74LVC245 /OE (0 = on); also ESP32 IO0
PC_DIR          equ     0x01    ; PC0: 74LVC245 direction (1 = toward ESP32)
MODE2           equ     0xC0    ; port A mode 2; PC0-PC2 outputs, all 0
; Left in port B by whatever sets up the card (card_on, fujinet-lib, FNON,
; FN.DVD, FNDISK). A reset makes port B an input that reads FF, and any
; other mode word clears it or makes it an input.
; FujiBus field descriptors: what follows the 6-byte header
FN_TIMEOUT      equ     2       ; no answer in time
FN_BAD          equ     3       ; bad length, checksum or device
NS_ERR          equ     3       ; byte: last error (1 = OK, 136 = EOF)
; A request block, read by fn_call, is two lines: what to send, then where
; the payload is and where the reply goes.
;   FNREQ  device, command, descriptor, aux1, aux2, aux3, aux4
;   FNBUF  payload, payload length, reply buffer, reply buffer size
; A program changes a block in place before a call (a length, a buffer):
RQ_AUX1         equ     3       ; aux1-aux4: the fields (a word at aux1-aux2,
RQ_AUX2         equ     4       ;   a long at aux1-aux4, low byte first)
macro FNREQ dev, cmd, desc, a1, a2, a3, a4
defb    dev, cmd, desc, a1, a2, a3, a4
macro FNBUF pay, plen, rep, rmax
; fujibus.inc -- FujiBus transactions over the H89 card's 82C55A.
; fn_call   HL -> a request block (FNREQ in fujinet.inc):
;           Sends the request in a SLIP frame, then takes the whole reply,
;           to its closing END, so the next request starts clean.
;   Exit:   A  = FN_OK (ACK), FN_NAK, FN_TIMEOUT or FN_BAD; Z set on FN_OK
;           BC = the reply's payload length (all of it, even past the buffer)
;           carry set if the payload was longer than the buffer (the rest
;           was dropped); fn_rep = the reply's 6-byte header;
;           fn_res and fn_len keep A and BC for later
; fn_raw    DE -> buffer, BC = its size. Takes whatever bytes come until
;           200 ms pass with none (the modem's replies are not framed).
; fn_send   HL -> a request block: sends it as fn_call does, but does not
;           wait for a reply. For the modem (50H), which answers in bare
;           bytes or not at all: take what comes with fn_raw.
;   Exit:   A = FN_OK, Z set; FN_TIMEOUT if the ESP32 did not take it.
; Forked from fujinet-h89's common/fujibus.inc: a request block instead of
; variables, replies of any length, NAK told apart from a bad frame.
TX_TIMEOUT      equ     500             ; 1 s for the ESP32 to take a byte
RX_FIRST        equ     7500            ; 15 s for the reply to begin
RX_TIMEOUT      equ     500             ; 1 s between reply bytes
RAW_FIRST       equ     1000            ; fn_raw: 2 s for the first byte
RAW_QUIET       equ     100             ; fn_raw: 200 ms of quiet ends it
ld      a,1                     ; send only: no reply to wait for
ld      (fn_sp),sp              ; a timeout returns from here
ld      a,(fn_dirty)            ; a call given up before: drain it
; the header: device, command, length, checksum 0, descriptor, aux
ld      e,a                     ; how many aux bytes it carries
ld      de,fn_out+6             ; aux1-aux4 (only n of them go)
ld      e,(hl)                  ; payload address and length
ld      e,(hl)                  ; reply buffer and its size
xor     a                       ; checksum over header, aux, payload
; send: one END, the packet, one END
ld      a,(fn_only)             ; fn_send: that is all
xor     a                       ; A = FN_OK, Z set, carry clear
; receive: wait for an END, skip any more, decode up to the next
ld      hl,0                    ; the reply's first byte is in A
ld      hl,(fn_idx)             ; at least a header,
ld      hl,(fn_idx)             ; as long as its header says,
ld      a,(fn_cks)              ; with its checksum right
cp      ACK                     ; an ACK, from the device asked
xor     a                       ; A = FN_OK, Z set, carry clear
; every way out: keep the result for later (fn_res, fn_len); flags kept
; BC = payload bytes received; fn_trunc = 1 if more than the buffer held
ex      de,hl                   ; HL = size, DE = received
sbc     hl,de                   ; size - received: borrow if short
; A reply byte: the first 6 to fn_rep, then into the reply buffer while it
; has room; every byte but the checksum's own goes into fn_cks
ld      a,h                     ; byte 4 is the checksum itself
ld      de,(fn_rmax)            ; payload byte, if there is room
; a timeout anywhere: give the call up (its reply may still be coming)
; D += BC bytes from HL: an 8-bit sum with end-around carry
; carry once (TICKS - fn_t0) has reached fn_tlim. Uses HL, DE.
; wait until the ESP32 has taken the last byte (/OBF high). Keeps BC DE HL.
; send A. Keeps BC, DE, HL.
; the next byte from the ESP32 into A. Keeps BC, DE, HL.
; after a call given up part way: take bytes until 100 ms pass with none
; (and at most 2048, in case a missing card reads as an endless stream)
; take unframed bytes into DE (BC = room) until RAW_QUIET ticks of quiet
jr      nc,fn_raw4              ; no room: count, drop
; aux bytes carried by each field descriptor, 0-7
fn_out:         defs    10              ; header (6) and aux (up to 4)
fn_res:         defb    0               ; the last call's result (A)
; card.inc -- start the H89 FujiNet card if nothing has yet (as FNON does),
; and face it toward us. From fujinet-h89's common/card.inc. Uses TICKS.
; The mark in port B and EN high mean something set the card up and nothing
; has reset the 82C55A since. EN alone can't tell: after a reset the 82C55A's
; bus hold can pull PC2 high while port A isn't in mode 2.
in      a,(PORTB)               ; set up since the last reset?
jr      nz,card_ready           ; yes, and running: leave it
ld      a,MODE2                 ; mode 2; PC0-PC2 out, all 0
ld      a,0x06                  ; EN=1, IO0=1 at once
ld      b,100                   ; about 200 ms with IO0 high
ld      a,SETUP_MARK            ; the card is set up
in      a,(PORTA)               ; drop a byte latched at start
; Is the card there, running and facing us? Z if so. Without a card the
; ports read FF, and every wait for a byte would see one at once, forever.
; Wait for the next 2 ms tick
; con.inc -- printing numbers and bytes on the console (built on conout).
;   phex8   A in hex          phex16  HL in hex
;   pdec8   A in decimal      pdec16  HL in decimal
;   pspace  one space         pip     HL -> 4 bytes as a dotted IP address
;   ptext   HL -> BC bytes as text, unprintable ones as '.'
;   pdump   HL -> BC bytes in hex, 16 to a line
;   phexs   HL -> BC bytes in hex on one line (at most 24, then "...")
;   getline HL -> buffer, B = its size: a line typed at the keyboard, shown
;           as it is typed (BACKSPACE and DELETE rub out), ended by RETURN;
;           stored NUL-terminated without the RETURN. Keeps HL.
;   strlen  HL -> a NUL-terminated string: BC = its length. Keeps HL.
; All keep BC, DE and HL unless they say otherwise.
ld      b,0                     ; digits printed so far
sbc     hl,de                   ; one too many: put it back
dec     b                       ; room for the NUL
jr      c,getl1                 ; other control characters: ignored
ld      a,c                     ; rub out the last one, if any
; tail.inc -- the library's data, the CP/M stack, and prog_end. Include it
; LAST, after your own code and data.
os_fptr:        defw    0               ; next byte to read from os_fbuf
os_feof:        defb    0               ; 1 = the file has ended
os_argp:        defw    0               ; SP at entry: the command line
os_consave:     defs    5               ; the console mode bytes at entry
os_hdefault:    defm    "SY0"           ; the default device, no extension
